findings.title: Auto scaling group in a single availability zone
findings.description: Group web-asg spans 3 availability zones.
findings.remediation: Add subnets from at least one more availability zone to the group. Spreading instances across zones costs nothing extra.

findings.title: Auto scaling group in a single availability zone
findings.description: Group worker-asg launches instances only in us-east-1a. If that zone has an outage the group cannot replace its instances anywhere else.
findings.remediation: Add subnets from at least one more availability zone to the group. Spreading instances across zones costs nothing extra.

findings.title: CloudTrail not enabled in all regions
findings.description: No multi-region trail is logging. API activity in regions you do not use goes unrecorded, which is where an attacker with stolen credentials tends to work, and there is no audit trail to investigate an incident with.
findings.remediation: Create a multi-region trail that delivers to an S3 bucket, with log file validation on, and make sure logging is started. The first copy of management events is free; you pay only for the S3 storage.

findings.title: DynamoDB table without point-in-time recovery
findings.description: Table orders has point-in-time recovery on.
findings.remediation: Enable point-in-time recovery under the table's Backups tab. It is billed per GB of table size per month, which is negligible for small tables.

findings.title: DynamoDB table without point-in-time recovery
findings.description: Table sessions has point-in-time recovery off. A buggy deploy that overwrites or deletes items cannot be rolled back to the moment before it ran.
findings.remediation: Enable point-in-time recovery under the table's Backups tab. It is billed per GB of table size per month, which is negligible for small tables.

findings.title: DynamoDB table without point-in-time recovery

findings.title: EBS default encryption off
findings.description: EBS encryption by default is off in eu-west-1. Any volume or snapshot created without an explicit encryption flag stores its data in plain text, and an unencrypted snapshot can be shared with other accounts.
findings.remediation: Turn on EBS encryption by default under EC2 > Settings > Data protection and security in each region. It is free with the AWS managed key and applies to new volumes only; existing unencrypted volumes must be copied to encrypted ones.

findings.title: EBS default encryption off
findings.description: New EBS volumes in us-east-1 are encrypted by default.
findings.remediation: Turn on EBS encryption by default under EC2 > Settings > Data protection and security in each region. It is free with the AWS managed key and applies to new volumes only; existing unencrypted volumes must be copied to encrypted ones.

findings.title: EBS default encryption off

findings.remediation: Turn on EBS encryption by default under EC2 > Settings > Data protection and security in each region. It is free with the AWS managed key and applies to new volumes only; existing unencrypted volumes must be copied to encrypted ones.

findings.title: gp2 volume that could be gp3
findings.description: Volume vol-961b37ffe7ebf4216 (8 GiB) is gp2. gp3 costs about 20% less per GiB and gives 3,000 IOPS at any size, where gp2 performance depends on volume size.
findings.remediation: Modify the volume and change its type to gp3. The change happens online with no downtime. For gp2 volumes larger than 1,000 GiB, set gp3 IOPS to match what gp2 provided (3 IOPS per GiB).

findings.title: EBS snapshot older than 90 days

findings.remediation: Delete snapshots you no longer need (a snapshot backing a registered AMI must have the AMI deregistered first). Use Data Lifecycle Manager to expire snapshots automatically, or move ones kept for compliance to the cheaper archive tier.

findings.title: GuardDuty not enabled
findings.description: GuardDuty is not enabled in eu-west-1. Nothing is watching CloudTrail, VPC flow and DNS logs there for signs of compromise such as crypto-mining or credentials used from an unusual place.
findings.remediation: Enable GuardDuty in every region, including unused ones, since that is where unexpected activity stands out. It has a 30-day free trial and is billed by the volume of logs analysed afterwards, so check the usage page before the trial ends.

findings.title: Access key older than 90 days
findings.description: Access key ending VOQ7 of user deploy-bot is 412 days old. Long-lived keys end up in shell history, CI logs and old laptops; the longer one lives, the more places it can leak from.
findings.remediation: Create a new key, switch the workload to it, deactivate the old key, and delete it once nothing breaks. Where possible replace the key with short-lived credentials: an IAM role for workloads, or `aws login` / IAM Identity Center for people.

findings.title: Root account without MFA
findings.description: The root user has no MFA device. Root cannot be restricted by IAM policies, so a stolen root password gives full control of the account, including billing and closing it.
findings.remediation: Sign in as the root user, open Security credentials and assign an MFA device (a passkey or hardware key is best). Then stop using root for daily work and keep it for the few tasks that require it.

findings.title: IAM user without MFA
findings.description: User amara.okafor has an MFA device.
findings.remediation: Have the user assign an MFA device under IAM > Users > Security credentials, or remove the console password if they do not need to sign in. Better still, move people to IAM Identity Center, which issues short-lived credentials.

findings.title: IAM user without MFA
findings.description: User daniel.reyes has an MFA device.
findings.remediation: Have the user assign an MFA device under IAM > Users > Security credentials, or remove the console password if they do not need to sign in. Better still, move people to IAM Identity Center, which issues short-lived credentials.

findings.title: IAM user without MFA
findings.description: User contractor-temp can sign in to the console with a password alone. A phished or reused password is then enough to act with all of this user's permissions.
findings.remediation: Have the user assign an MFA device under IAM > Users > Security credentials, or remove the console password if they do not need to sign in. Better still, move people to IAM Identity Center, which issues short-lived credentials.

findings.title: Lambda function without a dead-letter queue
findings.description: Function image-thumbnailer has no dead-letter queue or on-failure destination. An asynchronous event that still fails after Lambda's two retries is dropped without a trace.
findings.remediation: Add an SQS queue or SNS topic as the function's dead-letter queue, or an on-failure destination, and alarm on messages arriving there.

findings.title: Lambda function without a dead-letter queue
findings.description: Function nightly-export sends failed asynchronous events somewhere they can be seen.
findings.remediation: Add an SQS queue or SNS topic as the function's dead-letter queue, or an on-failure destination, and alarm on messages arriving there.

findings.title: CloudWatch log group with no retention set
findings.description: Log group /aws/lambda/image-thumbnailer never expires its logs. Stored log data is billed per GB every month and only ever grows.
findings.remediation: Set a retention period on the log group; 30 or 90 days suits most application logs. Set it in the Terraform or CloudFormation that creates the group so new groups do not default to never expiring.
